questions.statement: Excerpt: A brilliant show, funny from start to finish. Do not miss it. What is the tone?
questions.context: Lucia is reading a film blog that praises a new comedy warmly.

options.feedback: Correct! Enthusiastic correctly captures the glowing praise and strong recommendation, which shows the writer feels delighted and eager to convince readers.
The label critical is wrong for this extract because critical means focusing on faults and weaknesses, while the blog only offers warm praise without any complaint.
The label neutral is wrong here because neutral means presenting facts without feeling, whereas the blog uses emotional praise that clearly reveals personal delight.
The label bored is wrong because bored means uninterested and flat, which contradicts the lively adjectives and eager recommendation visible in the blog.

questions.explanation: Enthusiastic tone uses glowing adjectives like brilliant and unmissable plus exclamation and recommendation. Recognizing praise vocabulary helps learners separate genuine admiration from polite or neutral reporting in opinion texts.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: The battery is weak, the camera is disappointing, and the price is absurd. What is the tone?
questions.context: Diego is reading a phone review that lists faults in cold language.

options.feedback: The label enthusiastic is wrong because enthusiastic requires praise and excitement, while the review only lists defects and shows clear disappointment with the phone.
Correct! Critical correctly identifies the fault finding language and negative judgement, which proves the reviewer disapproves of the phone and warns readers.
The label neutral is wrong because neutral avoids judgement, whereas this review evaluates harshly and openly expresses dissatisfaction with the product.
The label nostalgic is wrong because nostalgic looks back fondly to the past, while the review focuses on present faults without any warm memory.

questions.explanation: A critical tone judges negatively with words like disappointing, flawed, and overpriced. Unlike neutral reporting, it evaluates and recommends against. Spotting evaluative adjectives is the fastest clue to criticism.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: The council met on Tuesday and approved the plan by 12 votes to 8. What is the tone?
questions.context: Carmen is reading a news report that only gives dates and numbers.

options.feedback: The label angry is wrong because angry needs strong negative emotion and blame, while the report stays calm and limits itself to dates and plain numbers.
The label ironic is wrong because ironic says the opposite of what is meant for effect, while this report means exactly what it states without wordplay.
Correct! Neutral correctly describes factual reporting without personal feeling, which matches a text that only presents dates, figures, and balanced verbs.
The label sarcastic is wrong because sarcastic mocks through cutting remarks, whereas the news text contains no mockery and maintains an impartial factual style.

questions.explanation: Neutral tone reports facts without adjectives of feeling or judgement. It uses numbers, dates, and balanced verbs like stated or reported. Absence of evaluative language distinguishes it from opinionated tones.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: What a wonderful traffic jam, another brilliant morning. What tone does the writer use?
questions.context: Pablo is reading a column that says the opposite of what it means.

options.feedback: The label sincere praise is wrong because sincere praise means the writer truly admires, while here the compliments clash with the described traffic chaos.
Correct! Ironic correctly captures saying the opposite for effect, because calling a traffic jam wonderful cannot be literal and clearly mocks the situation.
The label purely informative is wrong because purely informative gives neutral facts, whereas wonderful traffic jam adds an evaluative twist that signals mockery.
The label deeply nostalgic is wrong because deeply nostalgic recalls the past with warmth, while the column mocks a present failure without any longing.

questions.explanation: Ironic tone praises in words but blames in meaning, often about obvious failures. Clues include exaggerated compliments followed by negative facts. Readers must contrast literal words with the real situation described.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: This supposedly miracle method claims fluency in a week. Really? Which attitude fits best?
questions.context: Sara is reading an editorial that doubts a miracle study method.

options.feedback: The option fully trusting is wrong because fully trusting accepts claims without doubt, while the editorial questions the method and demands stronger proof.
The option openly hostile is wrong because openly hostile attacks with anger and insults, whereas the editorial doubts calmly and asks for evidence instead.
Correct! Skeptical correctly describes doubting the miracle claim until evidence appears, which matches the questioning words supposedly and claims in the text.
The option wildly enthusiastic is wrong because wildly enthusiastic celebrates without reservation, which contradicts the cautious doubt expressed toward the study method.

questions.explanation: Skeptical tone doubts claims and asks for evidence with words like supposedly, claims, and so called. It does not reject aggressively but suspends belief. Questioning language is the hallmark of healthy skepticism.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: Those golden summers in the village, long evenings by the river. What tone is this?
questions.context: Jorge is reading a travel article full of love for his village.

options.feedback: Correct! Nostalgic correctly reflects warm longing for past summers, because the phrases golden summers and long evenings idealize childhood village life.
The option fearful is wrong because fearful expresses worry about danger ahead, while the article glows with affection and shows no anxiety about the village.
The option dismissive is wrong because dismissive belittles something as unimportant, whereas the writer treasures every detail of village life with deep affection.
The option purely critical is wrong because purely critical focuses on faults, while the article celebrates the past warmly without judging or complaining.

questions.explanation: Nostalgic tone idealizes the past with warm memory words like those golden summers and we used to. It contrasts past warmth with present loss. Sensory detail about childhood is a strong signal of nostalgia.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Review A calls it cozy and delightful. Review B calls it noisy and rude. What contrast fits?
questions.context: Elena compares two reviews of the same restaurant with opposite feelings.

options.feedback: Correct! Positive versus negative correctly captures the contrast, because cozy and delightful praise the place while noisy and rude clearly condemn the same restaurant.
The option neutral versus neutral is wrong because neutral means no feeling, while both reviews use strong evaluative adjectives that reveal clear opposite feelings.
The option ironic versus literal is wrong because neither review says the opposite of its meaning, as both state their praise or complaint directly and sincerely.
The option formal versus informal is wrong because the difference here is feeling and judgement, not levels of formality or polite versus casual style.

questions.explanation: Comparing paired adjectives reveals tone contrast quickly. Warm words like cozy and delightful signal approval, while cold words like noisy and rude signal disapproval. Juxtaposing lexical sets trains readers to track stance shifts.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: Thanks so much for ignoring all our messages. What tone is the writer using?
questions.context: Raul is reading a letter that hides criticism behind polite smiles.

options.feedback: The label genuine thanks is wrong because genuine thanks expresses real gratitude, while the letter complains about being ignored and uses thanks as a weapon.
The label neutral report is wrong because neutral report avoids feeling, whereas the exaggerated politeness carries a clear bitter and mocking edge.
The label sincere apology is wrong because sincere apology admits fault and seeks forgiveness, while the writer blames the reader and offers no regret.
Correct! Sarcastic correctly identifies polite words used to criticize, because thanking someone for ignoring every message can only be bitter mockery.

questions.explanation: Sarcastic tone uses polite wording to wound, with exaggeration like thanks so much for ignoring us. Context of complaint exposes the bite. Learners must weigh situation against literal politeness to detect sarcasm.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence shows a cautious tone about a possible danger?
questions.context: Nora is studying which sentence signals worry in an opinion text.

options.text: The river may flood unless barriers improve.
options.feedback: The sentence about risks is correct because warning that the river may flood unless barriers improve expresses careful concern rather than certainty or celebration.

options.text: The festival was joyful and bright.
options.feedback: The option The festival was joyful and bright is wrong because joyful and bright express celebration, which contains no warning or careful concern about danger.

options.text: Everyone agrees the plan is perfect.
options.feedback: The option Everyone agrees the plan is perfect is wrong because perfect agreement shows total confidence, which is opposite to the careful doubt of caution.
The option The results prove total success is wrong because prove total success claims certain triumph, while cautious tone stresses possible danger and needed care.

questions.explanation: Cautious tone warns with hedges like may, might, risks, and unless we act. It advises care without panic. Modal verbs plus risk vocabulary reliably mark caution in editorials and reports.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: Free buses are essential and fairer for all families. What stance does the writer take?
questions.context: Iker is reading an essay that strongly supports free school buses.

options.feedback: The label opposed is wrong because opposed argues against a proposal, while the essay lists benefits of buses and urges the council to fund them.
The label undecided is wrong because undecided balances both sides without choice, whereas the essay takes a clear side and pushes for free buses.
Correct! Supportive correctly names arguing in favor with benefits, because calling buses essential and fairer shows the writer champions the proposal actively.
The label mocking is wrong because mocking ridicules through scorn, while the essay treats buses seriously and argues with respectful benefit language.

questions.explanation: Supportive tone argues in favor with benefit language like essential, fairer, and helps families. It proposes action rather than merely describing. Benefit plus proposal structure marks advocacy clearly.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The review praises one phone as perfect and never mentions its faults. What is this called?
questions.context: Marta is checking whether a review is balanced or one sided.

options.feedback: Correct! Biased correctly means favoring one phone while hiding its flaws, because praising only one model with superlatives and silence reveals unfair preference.
The option balanced is wrong because balanced weighs both strengths and weaknesses fairly, while the review praises one phone and ignores its obvious drawbacks.
The option neutral is wrong because neutral reports without taking sides, whereas the review clearly champions one brand with loaded and selective praise.
The option purely descriptive is wrong because purely descriptive lists features factually, while the review evaluates with glowing adjectives that push one choice.

questions.explanation: Biased tone favors one side by hiding drawbacks and using loaded praise only for its choice. Balanced writing admits limits on both sides. Spotting one sided superlatives without concessions reveals bias fast.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: Although the app is slow at times, it remains useful. What tone is this?
questions.context: Alba reads a paragraph where the author admits a small fault politely.

options.feedback: The option furious attack is wrong because furious attack uses violent blame and insults, while the paragraph admits limits calmly with polite concession language.
Correct! Measured correctly describes calm and balanced judgement, because admitting a small fault with although shows fairness rather than rage or blind praise.
The option wild celebration is wrong because wild celebration praises without reserve, whereas the author qualifies approval by openly recognizing a weakness.
The option total indifference is wrong because total indifference shows no interest at all, while the author cares enough to weigh strengths against weaknesses.

questions.explanation: Measured tone concedes limits with softeners like although, however, and to some extent. It stays fair while still judging. Concession plus calm evaluation marks thoughtful and moderate opinion writing.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: Plastic is choking our seas. We must act now before it is too late. What is the tone?
questions.context: Hugo reads an opinion piece full of urgent warnings about plastic.

options.feedback: The label relaxed is wrong because relaxed suggests calm acceptance, while the piece uses crisis language and urgent calls that demand immediate action now.
The label amused is wrong because amused finds something funny, whereas the article treats plastic pollution as a serious emergency without any humor.
Correct! Alarmed correctly captures urgent warning about a crisis, because phrases like before it is too late create pressure for immediate action.
The label nostalgic is wrong because nostalgic longs for the past warmly, while the piece fears the future and pushes readers to act against plastic waste.

questions.explanation: Alarmed tone stresses urgency with words like crisis, now, before it is too late. It demands immediate action. Time pressure vocabulary plus imperatives distinguishes alarm from calm caution.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: The wait was the worst in human history, a total disaster. What tone is used?
questions.context: Leire studies how exaggeration changes the tone of a complaint.

options.feedback: The option literal and precise is wrong because literal and precise sticks to verifiable facts, while worst meal in human history wildly exaggerates beyond any proof.
Correct! Hyperbolic correctly names deliberate exaggeration for effect, because calling a slow meal the worst in human history inflates annoyance into comedy.
The option neutral and factual is wrong because neutral and factual avoids evaluation, whereas total disaster judges emotionally with extreme and unmeasured language.
The option gently supportive is wrong because gently supportive encourages kindly, while the sentence attacks the restaurant with sweeping and hostile overstatement.

questions.explanation: Hyperbolic tone inflates with extremes like worst ever and total disaster. It vents feeling rather than informing precisely. Absolute superlatives without evidence signal comic or angry overstatement.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Headline A: A green jewel for the city. Headline B: A concrete waste of money. What contrast fits?
questions.context: Mario reads two headlines about the same new park and compares stance.

options.feedback: Correct! Celebratory versus disapproving correctly maps the contrast, because green jewel praises the park while concrete waste condemns the same project as misuse.
The option both neutral is wrong because both neutral would require plain facts, while jewel and waste are loaded evaluations that reveal opposite feelings.
The option both humorous is wrong because both humorous would need jokes or wordplay, whereas the headlines judge seriously with praise versus blame.
The option both nostalgic is wrong because both nostalgic would recall the past fondly, while the headlines evaluate a present park without any backward longing.

questions.explanation: Headline diction reveals stance. Green jewel celebrates value, while concrete waste condemns cost. Noun phrases carry judgement even without verbs. Tracking positive versus negative images unlocks headline tone.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: Superb acting, yet a weak and predictable plot. What best describes the tone?
questions.context: Clara reads a review that mixes praise for acting with dislike of plot.

options.feedback: The label purely negative is wrong because purely negative allows no praise, while the review admires the acting warmly even as it rejects the weak plot.
The label purely positive is wrong because purely positive allows no complaint, whereas the review clearly criticizes the slow and predictable story.
Correct! Mixed correctly describes praising one element while criticizing another, because superb acting yet weak plot balances admiration against clear disappointment.
The label completely indifferent is wrong because completely indifferent shows no feeling, while the review expresses strong admiration and strong annoyance together.

questions.explanation: Mixed tone balances praise and criticism with contrast markers like yet, but, and despite. It shows nuanced judgement rather than simple love or hate. But structures are reliable signs of two sided evaluation.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Excerpt: You have the talent and the energy to build a brighter future. What is the tone?
questions.context: Adrian reads a speech that encourages teens with strong hopeful words.

options.feedback: The label pessimistic is wrong because pessimistic expects failure and gloom, while the speech stresses opportunity and confident belief in teen ability.
The label cynical is wrong because cynical distrusts motives and mocks effort, whereas the speech trusts teens and urges them to shape a brighter future.
The label resigned is wrong because resigned accepts defeat passively, while the speech calls for energetic action and hopeful commitment to change.
Correct! Optimistic correctly captures hopeful encouragement about the future, because opportunity and we can inspire confidence rather than fear or doubt.

questions.explanation: Optimistic tone inspires with future oriented lexis like opportunity, we can, brighter tomorrow. It acknowledges problems but stresses agency. Hope plus action verbs marks constructive optimism in speeches.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The library opened in 2019. It is a wonderful success. The two sentences are what?
questions.context: Aitor studies a paragraph where facts and opinions are woven together.

options.feedback: Correct! Fact plus opinion correctly splits the paragraph, because opened in 2019 is verifiable history while wonderful success adds personal judgement that cannot be proved.
The option two facts is wrong because two facts would both be verifiable, while wonderful success expresses evaluation rather than checkable data.
The option two opinions is wrong because two opinions would both be judgements, whereas opened in 2019 states a date that can be verified objectively.
The option question plus answer is wrong because question plus answer needs an interrogative, while the paragraph contains two statements and no question at all.

questions.explanation: Fact states verifiable data like opened in 2019, while opinion adds judgement like wonderful success. Modal plus adjective test separates them. B2 readers must split objective clauses from evaluative clauses inside one paragraph.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The editorial lists harm to farms but never praises the dam directly. What is the hidden stance?
questions.context: Nerea reads a long editorial and must infer the hidden position of the author.

options.feedback: The option openly in favor is wrong because openly in favor states support directly, while the author never praises the dam and only stresses its serious harms.
The option strictly neutral is wrong because strictly neutral balances benefits and harms evenly, whereas the editorial selects only damage and faint praise for builders.
Correct! Quietly opposed correctly infers hidden resistance, because emphasizing harm to farms while giving only faint polite credit reveals underlying disapproval of the dam.
The option openly mocking is wrong because openly mocking uses sarcasm and ridicule, while the editorial stays serious and lets careful selection imply its quiet opposition.

questions.explanation: Implicit stance hides in selection and irony rather than direct I oppose. Praising opponents weakly while detailing harms signals quiet opposition. Tracking what is emphasized versus minimized reveals the true position.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which clue most reliably reveals the overall tone of an opinion text?
questions.context: Unai must choose the most reliable clue when judging tone under exam pressure.

options.feedback: The option a single exclamation mark is wrong because a single exclamation mark can show excitement, alarm, or irony, so alone it cannot reliably prove any particular overall tone.
The option the length of the text is wrong because the length of the text measures quantity rather than attitude, so long or short passages can share the same tone.
The option the font of the article is wrong because the font of the article is a visual design choice that carries no reliable information about author attitude or stance.
Correct! Repeated evaluative language plus purpose correctly gives the safest evidence, because consistent adjectives and the call to action confirm stance beyond isolated words.

questions.explanation: Reliable tone clues combine repeated evaluative adjectives with rhetorical purpose across the whole text. Single words can mislead through irony, but consistent lexical sets plus call to action confirm stance. This meta skill prevents hasty judgement from isolated phrases.
questions.subject: ingles
